name: Centro Historico
tagline: The UNESCO colonial heart of Paraty
description: The preserved old town of whitewashed colonial houses, colourful doors and irregular cobbled streets that flood at high tide. It is the atmospheric core, packed with restaurants, galleries, pousadas and craft shops, and the liveliest part of town for visitors.
bestFor: Culture lovers and short stays wanting charm, cafes and walkability
cons: Pricier and busiest in high season

name: Praia do Pontal and Jabaquara
tagline: Beach neighbourhoods just across the river
description: Sitting just over the river from the old town, these areas offer easy beach access, a more everyday local feel and quieter streets. Praia do Pontal has casual beach bars, while Jabaquara stretches to a broad, calm beach popular with families and longer-stay visitors.
bestFor: Longer stays wanting beach access, calm and better-value accommodation
pros: Short walk to the old town

name: Cabore
tagline: Waterfront point beside the old town
description: A small point on the water's edge next to the historic centre, Cabore is known for its riverside setting, seafood spots and a laid-back gathering place where locals and visitors watch the boats. It blends old-town proximity with a slightly calmer, open waterfront feel.
bestFor: Those wanting old-town access with river views and a quieter edge
cons: Busy when the centre is crowded

name: Trindade and the beach road
tagline: Outlying beaches and waterfalls south of town
description: Down the coastal road towards the mountains lies Trindade, a rustic beach village framed by rainforest and natural pools, along with turn-offs to inland waterfalls and cachaca distilleries. It is a scenic, back-to-nature base well beyond the polished old town.
bestFor: Nature seekers happy to trade convenience for beaches and rainforest
cons: Needs a car or bus to get around
